source: Chronicling America (via loc.gov + tile.loc.gov ALTO side-door; legacy API dead)
method_note: WebFetch 403 on loc.gov; used curl + the tile.loc.gov word-coordinates-service to recover verbatim OCR snippets. Collection q= is loose OR-match, so high counts are corpus noise; only items whose OCR literally contained a Hubbell token were kept.
result: NULL for Charles across all three angles. Every Hubbell OCR hit is a documented namesake.
namesakes_found: GEO. C. HUBBEL & Co. — NYC patent-collar / 'HUBBEL'S GOLDEN BITTERS' advertiser (repeated).
Maj. Wilson Hubbell, 62nd NY ('Anderson Zouaves') — incl. an 1864 death notice (NOT Charles).
Frederick M. Hubbell — Des Moines financier, as 'Polk & Hubbell' abstract books (Knoxville [IA] Journal 1876) — confirms F.M. Hubbell IS already prominent by 1875-76.
Jay A. Hubbell (Michigan/Iowa congressman); J. B. Hubbell (Ohio congressman); E. N. Hubbell of Coxsackie; Levi Hubbell (WI); Charles W. Hubbell (NYC Mason).
structural_gap: The papers that would carry (a) a 153rd-NY soldier-correspondent letter and (b) an Eastern death notice — Plattsburgh Republican/Sentinel, Montgomery County Republican/Fonda papers — are NOT in Chronicling America at all (they live at NYS Historic Newspapers). Pocahontas Co. Iowa papers appear undigitized. So the NULL reflects coverage, not absence.
brother_james_note: James Hubbell (also Co. I) likewise did not surface — consistent with the regiment's NY home papers being absent from this corpus.
same_town_namesake_check: F. M. Hubbell (Iowa) and the GEO. C. HUBBEL advertiser ruled out; brother James not falsely attributed.
